# Code of conduct

## Our pledge

We as members, contributors, and maintainers pledge to make participation in the Picteus community a welcoming, constructive, and harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

---

## Community standards

### Positive behavior

Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment include:

- **Empathy & kindness**: being gentle, empathetic, and considerate of others at all times ;
- **Respect**: respecting differing opinions, viewpoints, and levels of technical experience ;
- **Constructive feedback**: offering and gracefully accepting constructive feedback ;
- **Responsibility**: taking responsibility for mistakes, offering sincere apologies when appropriate, and learning from the experience ;
- **Community focus**: focusing on what is best not only for oneself as an individual, but for the community and project as a whole.

### Communication guidelines

To foster thoughtful and effective technical collaboration:

- **Provide context and technical details**: keep in mind that most people — including the maintainers and primary contributors — are not telepathic. Always provide adequate context, clear explanations, reproduction steps, and relevant system details when opening issues, asking questions, or proposing changes ;
- **Avoid instant messaging communication styles**: avoid fragmented, rushed, or "WhatsApp-style" messaging — such as single-line bursts, cryptic abbreviations, or casual messaging jargon. Contributors are encouraged to take the time to compose well-structured, clear, and articulated messages in issues, pull requests, and discussions.

### Unacceptable behavior

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

- The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind ;
- Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks ;
- Public or private harassment ;
- Publishing others' private information — such as a physical or email address — without their explicit permission ;
- Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional open-source setting.

---

## Enforcement responsibilities

Community maintainers are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Maintainers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, pull requests, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned with this code of conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

---

## Scope

This code of conduct applies within all community spaces — including the Picteus GitHub repository, issue tracker, pull requests, and discussions —, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the project in public spaces.

---

## Contact & reporting

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported directly to the maintainers by emailing:

[contact@picteus.com](mailto:contact@picteus.com)

All reports will be reviewed promptly, fairly, and with strict confidentiality. Maintainers are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.
